sense.text:
The ADL, the SPLC, these Jewish organizations say that we’re crazy, we’re a cult. Well, if we’re crazy and a cult, why are you so bothered? Why does it upset you so much? Paul had to deal with that. The Sadducees thought there is no resurrection, and both the Sadducees and the Pharisees believed that Christ was not the Son of the Most High.

“Now if Christ be preached that he rose from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?” They say that.

“But if there be no resurrection of the dead, then is Christ not risen”. “And if Christ be not risen”, if Christ did not rise from the dead, “then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.” Our preaching is a waste of time.

So why does it trouble you so? Paul was getting on them: what are you upset for? If Christ did not rise from the dead and he’s not the Son of God, why are you so upset? Why does it bother you that this little cult, what they call a cult, believes in this?

“And we are found false witnesses of God; because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead rise not.” “For if the dead rise not, then is not Christ raised: And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.”

Paul was getting on them: you don’t believe in Christ, so why does it bother you that we teach about Christ resurrecting? It just disturbs you. And you know why it disturbs them? Because it’s true. If we’re so nuts, so crazy, why does it bother the ADL? If we’re not the Jews the Bible speaks of, why does it upset them so much? Because they know what we’re saying is the truth. If Christ ain’t black, what you mad for? Because you know it’s true.

This is the gospel being preached, the first link in the chain of events that leads to our deliverance: the gospel preached to Israel, then the economic reset, then tribulation, then war, Armageddon, then deliverance.

Christ said “Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost”. That’s the verse Christians use to say the gospel is for everybody. But Christ said teach all nations because the Israelites would be scattered in all nations. Going back to it after the precepts: now we understand what he means, because the Israelites would be scattered in all nations.
“Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you”.

precepts.why: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations”: the Israelites would be scattered. That’s the prophecy, and this is why Christ said go and teach all nations, because the Israelites would be scattered in all nations. “And ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Wood and stone: Islam and Christianity, the two major religions of our people.
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven”: out of every nation, because we were scattered in all nations.
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. We were scattered in all nations; that’s who Christ sent them to teach.

Brothers, sisters, we’re going to succeed no matter what the white man does, and here’s the evidence: “After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands”.

So who was this great number of people of all nations and kindreds and tongues? The Israelites, gathered out of all the nations they were scattered in. We are going to succeed; it’s already written. So never doubt, never give up.

sense.text:
“And I beheld, and lo a black horse”: this black horse represents the dark nations. “And he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand”. The World Bank and the IMF, the International Monetary Fund, are the organizations that deal unjustly economically, and they’re all located in Washington DC, right across the street from each other.

Now there’s something called BRICS: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, and they’re backing it with gold and silver. Saudi Arabia wants to join now too. Don’t think the beast sleeps on stuff like this; they see what’s happening. A couple of things could happen. America could say, we’re going to shut this down, and drop a bomb on it. Or America could say, let it ride, let it affect everything globally so people fall economically, and then bring in their new digital currency and blame all the famine and problems on BRICS: everybody followed Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa and that new monetary thing, and look what happened, the world’s economy collapsed. Then the white man comes and saves the day. There’s a couple of things this guy could do. He is the devil the Bible speaks of; make no ifs, ands or buts about it.

“A measure of wheat for a penny”: that’s how much wheat should cost, a measure of wheat for a penny, “and three measures of barley for a penny”. “And see thou hurt not the oil and the wine”: don’t be unjust.

The ones that hurt the oil and the wine, the ones that are unjust, are the IMF and the World Bank, right across the street from one another. That’s all Esau; America controls all of that. They’re the ones that dictate how much a continent’s or a country’s money is worth. They’re the ones that tell Africa: although you have all the natural resources and the world depends on you, your money’s value is garbage, it’s nothing. No ifs, ands or buts about it: the beast has spoken.

So the Bible’s letting you know: don’t think BRICS is going to outsmart this beast. They’re not going to outsmart this man. This beast is the eighth head, and all nations submit to him. Russia is going to outsmart America? No they’re not; it’s not going to happen.

Still dealing with the economy. “And he causeth all, both small and great”: this he is this white man here in America. “Rich and poor, free and bond”: the free countries and the third world countries, that’s the free and bond.

“To receive a mark”: that mark represents sin. Write that down: the mark is sin, that’s all it is, to make it plain for you. Whether it’s in the realm of politics or religion, it’s still sin. They’re going to create something to have us go against the word of God. “In their right hand”: people are going to support it; “or in their foreheads”: you’re going to believe it.

“And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark”: they’re going to control the monetary system, which means it’s going to go somehow digital. When a nation goes against America they enforce sanctions and embargoes; we see that on a global scale. But on an individual scale, didn’t we just see that with Andrew Tate? And with Wendy Williams: they shut all her bank accounts down because she didn’t want to go along with the program. We’re seeing little glimpses of it. Don’t think this man does not have the technology to hit each of us individually: what did he say, Jesus is black? Shut his bank account down. Shazam, your bank account’s shut down, everything.

“He that had the mark”: their sin nature, that sin doctrine in their head. “Or the name of the beast”: America, Babylon the great. “Or the number of his name”: that goes into 666. “Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man”: this number represents the white man. It’s not an individual man; don’t go looking in the back of somebody’s head from them stupid movies. No, the Bible’s talking about a race of men: it’s Esau, Edom, that’s who it is.

So there’s going to be an economic change where they’re going to control everything, and they’re going to use that to manipulate us, to try to get us to stop preaching the gospel. Some of you are going to give in, because of my wife, my children. Although we receive thousands of Israelites, I pray you do, but some of you are just here.

They don’t know the scriptures like we know the scriptures. “Neither hoped they for the wages of righteousness, nor discerned a reward for blameless souls.”

“So shall I be saved from mine enemies” goes with Luke: “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies”. We stress the we: “and from the hand of all that hate us”. We’re going to be saved from this white man and all his allies.

So the I there that David is talking about in Psalms 18:3 is the we in Luke.

sense.text: “Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations also of the hills moved and were shaken, because he was wroth”. This is prophetic for us. Didn’t we just read that in Revelation 6, the earth shaking and the stars falling from heaven, and the nations saying fall on us, hide us from the face of him that sits on the throne? Every island and every mountain moved: it’s saying the same thing.
“There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, and fire out of his mouth devoured: coals were kindled by it.” Destruction is coming.

“He bowed the heavens also, and came down”: this didn’t happen during the time of David; the Lord didn’t come down during the time of David. “And darkness was under his feet”: that’s what we just read in Revelation 6, fall on us and hide us from him that sits on the throne. Christ was coming; the Lord was coming.
“And he rode upon a cherub”: that’s that chariot. “And did fly: yea, he did fly upon the wings of the wind.”

“He made darkness his secret place; his pavilion round about him were dark waters and thick clouds of the skies. At the brightness that was before him his thick clouds passed, hail stones and coals of fire.” So when the Lord comes back it’s going to be thunder, lightning, destruction. “The Lord also thundered in the heavens, and the Highest gave his voice; hail stones and coals of fire. Yea, he sent out his arrows, and scattered them; and he shot out lightnings, and discomfited them.”

“Then the channels of waters were seen, and the foundations of the world were discovered”. Imagine that when the Lord comes back: imagine the oceans separate so you could see the bottom of the sea. Everything’s going to be moved when the Lord comes back; nothing’s going to stay in its place.

“He sent from above, he took me, he drew me out of many waters.” He took me: what does the church call that? The rapture. Whatever troubles, the Lord said, I got you.

This is what the world is afraid of: the deliverance of the Israelites. They’re afraid, and they need to be afraid.

“He delivered me from my strong enemy”: the white man is the strong enemy. He’s got the missiles, he’s got the bombs, he’s got the technology. All we got is the Bible, but that’s all we need. “And from them which hated me: for they were too strong for me. They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the Lord was my stay.”

“He brought me forth also into a large place”. A lot of times we said, where’s the Lord going to take us? David is telling you right there: he took me and brought me to a large place. Write this down: the wilderness. “He delivered me, because he delighted in me.”

precepts.why: He took me: we’re coming back. “And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” That’s the Lord sending from above and taking his elect.

We’re going to read the whole chapter later, but just for the point: “Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people”. He ain’t coming for the salvation of all races on Earth; he’s coming for the salvation of his people. “Even for salvation with thine anointed”: that’s it right there. “Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: that’s the war; he’s going to kill a whole lot of people.

“Gather my saints together unto me”: this is the rapture, what they call the rapture. He’s not gathering all nations on the planet Earth; he says gather my saints together unto me, “those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” And in case you’re that stupid: the only ones that made a covenant with God by sacrifice were the twelve tribes of Israel.

The world needs to be afraid of the deliverance of the Israelites. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness”: that’s what’s happening now. “Before the face of such as have afflicted him”: the white man afflicted Rasheem Carter, the white man afflicted Breonna Taylor, the white man afflicted Michael Stewart. It’s always that damn white man afflicting us, from sun up to sundown, day after day, week after week, month after month, year after year. Now it’s our time to rise.

“And made no account of his labours”: y’all ready for the reparations? The Bible says they made no account of our labors. No matter how much work we did in this country, they said we don’t give a damn.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”: that’s what’s happening now. “And shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation”: this is the strangeness of our salvation, our deliverance.

sense.text: That large place David was brought forth into. “As I live, saith the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you”.

“And I will bring you out from the people”: this is the deliverance. “And will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered”: all the countries we were scattered in. He said I’m going to deliver the Israelites. “With a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out”: you see that fury? The Lord ain’t going to play with none of us.
“And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.” He’s going to talk with us face to face.
“Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”: he’s telling you what the wilderness is; he’s telling you where the wilderness is.

precepts.why:
Face to face: Paul told us about this. “For now we see through a glass, darkly”: right now we see through a glass darkly; we don’t never claim to know everything. “But then face to face”: then, in the wilderness, face to face.

“Now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” In the wilderness he’s going to reveal who we are. That part right there is a heavy meaning; we never really touch on that too much, but it’s heavy. Say you’ve got Deacon Malachi here: that’s how we know him. On that day, when we are speaking with the Lord face to face, he’s going to reveal who everybody is from the beginning, what your real name is. You might think your name is Shaniqua or Ray Ray; he’s going to give you your true name, and we’re all going to see from the beginning. God knows us from the beginning, and we’re going to know from that far back.

Paul said the same thing about the wilderness: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” He’s talking about back then, when we were in the wilderness, and he says that’s an example to us. When you read the chapter, he goes step by step through things that occurred in the wilderness with Moses.

Paul sums it up: “Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come”. Because then we are at the end of the world: what happened to our fathers in the wilderness of Egypt is written for us, who will be brought into the wilderness of the people.

sense.text: “A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth. O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years”. Guess who that work is: us. He’s reviving us. “In wrath remember mercy”.

“God came from Teman”: it’s about Christ. “And the Holy One from mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens”: this is the same thing as in Matthew 24, the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. “And the earth was full of his praise.”

“And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand”: there’s a power emanating from his hands. That’s where you get all these cartoons from; they get it from the word of God, the Bible. There’s going to be power coming out of the Lord’s hand.

“And there was the hiding of his power”: remember, Christ created everything, remember John chapter 1. He’s going to hide some of his power; that’s what he’s saying.
“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet”: destruction comes forth at his feet.

“He stood, and measured the earth”: Christ is going to stand and measure the earth, the circumference of the earth: how much power is required to destroy these nations. “He beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.”
“I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction”: the tents of Cushan is Ethiopia. “And the curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.”

“Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” When the Bible talks about water, sometimes it’s making reference to people. The rivers are nations: “was thine anger against the rivers?” Nations. “Was thy wrath against the sea”: people, nations. “That thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?”

“Thy bow was made quite naked”: the bow is an instrument of war. The bow it’s talking about, made quite naked, is the word of God, because it’s obvious the Lord is coming back for war. All through the Bible it says God’s coming back for war. Christianity don’t teach that; they say he’s coming back for love and hugs and kisses. That’s not biblical.

“According to the oaths of the tribes, even thy word”: that’s the proof that the bow it’s talking about is the word of God. Believe it or not, this Bible is the oaths of the tribes of Israel. This Bible is not the oath of Esau; it is not the oath of the Philistines or the Jebusites or the Moabites. This Bible is the oath of the twelve tribes of Israel. “Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.”

“The mountains saw thee, and they trembled: the overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice, and lifted up his hands on high.” Now this is the literal waters, the oceans going up high, like we read earlier about the channels of the waters being seen: that’s what this is talking about.
“The sun and moon stood still in their habitation”: that’s some heavy stuff, like during the time of Joshua. “At the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear.”

“Thou didst march through the land in indignation”: righteous anger. “Thou didst thresh the heathen in anger”: the word heathen means nation. He’s going to thresh the heathen, the nations, in anger. Not love: anger.

“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people”: he’s only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel; the Lord is coming back to save us. “Even for salvation with thine anointed”: that’s Christ.

“Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: now we know who the head of the wicked is; the head out of the house of the wicked is Idumea. “By discovering the foundation unto the neck”: you cut somebody’s neck and the head comes off. America’s the head of all these nations.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: the nations are going to come out as a whirlwind to try to scatter the Son of God and his angels.

“Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: the rejoicing of the nations was as to devour the poor secretly.

precepts.why: So when Christ comes: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”. “And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”: we’re going to cry. “And they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” That is God coming from Teman, his glory covering the heavens.

This explains the rivers. “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” So when the Bible talks about water, sometimes it’s making reference to people.

“And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.” That’s the proof that waters are sometimes referenced as people. So when the Lord is displeased against the rivers and his wrath is against the sea, it’s against the nations.
He’s only coming to save the twelve tribes of Israel: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.”

Who is the head of the wicked? “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”. Look up Idumea: pertaining to Edom, the Greek and Roman name for Edom. Christians say Idumea has been destroyed already. Really? Then Christ don’t know what he’s talking about? Idumea is all Caucasians: that’s America, that’s Russia, that’s Germany, France, Britain. That’s Idumea.

So what are you all marrying them for, sisters and brothers? You’re going to get put to death with them; ashes to ashes for you. Christ is coming back to destroy them. This ain’t no racist rant; this is all Bible. Bring us to a court of law: that’s what the Bible says, freedom of speech, we’re going to read what the Bible says.

“And upon the people of my curse”: they are the people of God’s curse, “to judgment.”

The nations coming out as a whirlwind to scatter: “And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.” This is the proof that when Christ comes back there’s going to be war already on Earth.

“And an innumerable multitude shall be gathered together, as thou sawest them, willing to come, and to overcome him by fighting”: they’re going to try to fight the Son of God. “But he shall stand upon the top of the mount Sion. And Sion shall come, and shall be shewed to all men”: that’s us, “being prepared and builded, like as thou sawest the hill graven without hands.”

“And this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations”: he don’t care about the ICBM missiles and all their various technology. He’s going to rebuke every invention they got; their space force will be crushed and destroyed. “And shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented”: they tormented us; Christ is going to torment them. “And he shall destroy them without labour”.

What does it mean, their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly? “Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the Lord”: they have think tanks where they sit around and discuss how to destroy the Israelites. “And their works are in the dark, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us?” Who’s going to know that we’re sitting here plotting and planning against the twelve tribes of Israel: poisoning food, giving them rap music, destroying their families through welfare and making it sound like we’re trying to help them, guns and drugs and things of that nature.
We read it earlier, but in case y’all forgot: “The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth.” That plotting is the devouring of the poor secretly.

This happened during the time of Persia, but it’s relevant for us today; the Bible is very relevant. “But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building”. “And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions”: they get public opinion; they try to get the people in mobs against us. “They hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived”. They did it back then, and they’re doing it now, today.

sense.text: “He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High”: we’ve got to dwell in this Bible. “Shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty”: his protection.
“I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.”

“Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler”: the fowler is a bird catcher. That represents the white man, the traps that he has out in his system. “And from the noisome pestilence”: disease.
“He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.” His truth means his laws: God’s laws are our protection.
“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day”: these are the arrows that fly by day. When the missiles come, we’re going to look up and smile.
“Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday”: it’s telling us when destruction is coming: at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side”: we’re going to see a thousand people falling at our side, “and ten thousand at thy right hand”: we’re going to see ten thousand people drop dead on our right side. “But it shall not come nigh thee”: it’s not going to come near the elect that’s alive at that time.
“Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked”: you’re going to see the reward of the wicked.

precepts.why: The secret place of the Most High: “The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever”. So the secret things belong to the Most High, and he reveals them to the Israelites and to our children. That’s why the nations don’t understand the mysteries of God.
“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” When the prophets bring out the secrets of the Lord, that’s when the angels are activated.

This precept is for Psalms 91:6, the destruction that wasteth at noonday. “For Gaza shall be forsaken”: Gaza is under Palestinian control, and Gaza shall be destroyed. God is telling you he’s going to destroy Gaza. “And Ashkelon a desolation”: Ashkelon is up above it on the map; it shall be decimated by God. “They shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day”: Ashdod is right above Ashkelon. “And Ekron shall be rooted up”: Ekron is further to the side, right next to Ashdod.

So it’s already laid out on the map. God’s got it written in the Bible: I’m going to destroy these places. The church is playing games, and Islam ain’t going to tell you a damn thing, but it’s in the Bible.

Those that are alive at that time will only see; they’re going to see the destruction on their left hand and on their right hand. Here’s the proof: “And it shall come to pass, that in all the land, saith the Lord”: that’s here in America, “two parts therein shall be cut off and die”. That’s your mothers, your fathers, your uncles, those Israelites that rebel against the laws of God: that’s two out of three Israelites. “But the third shall be left therein”: that’s one out of three.

“And I will bring the third part through the fire”: that’s what David said in Psalms 91, through the fire, and that’s literal fire as well. “And will refine them as silver is refined”: that’s us, that change in the twinkling of an eye. “And will try them as gold is tried”: that’s why Paul said remember what happened in the wilderness, because when we get back there we’re going to be tried again. “They shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people: and they shall say, The Lord is my God.” You’re going to say the Lord is my God.

sense.text:
When it says we shall be refined as silver, here it is. “Awake to righteousness, and sin not”: stop. That’s a message for all of us; we better awake. It’s for you men and women out there doing secret sins: y’all better stop it. You’re being warned right now, and you know who you are.

“For some have not the knowledge of God”: some of you in here don’t have the knowledge of God, some of you listening don’t have the knowledge of God, because if you did you’d stop sinning. “I speak this to your shame”: he’s talking to the Corinthians, which is us.
“But some man will say, How are the dead raised up? and with what body do they come?” The Corinthians were always challenging Paul: what kind of body are they going to have when they get raised up?
“Thou fool”: you idiot. What you put in the ground is not quickened except it die first.

Paul gives an example. Put a mustard seed on the screen: y’all see that mustard seed on the tip of that Edomite’s finger. Then the mustard plant, the mustard tree: it’s still small, but it grows really big. Go back to the seed and zoom in: that shell has to be destroyed.

“That which thou sowest, thou sowest not that body that shall be”: what you’re sowing in the earth is not that body that shall be. That’s the husk, the shell. The first thing it’s in has to die, then what it really is has to come out. Paul is comparing you and me to that seed. This body that we’re in is that seed; this ain’t the real us, this is just the husk.
“And to every seed his own body”: every one of us got our own body.

“All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds.” That kills evolution. They say we all came from a monkey and it changed into all these different things. No.
Celestial means angelic bodies, God bodies. Terrestrial is what we got now: terrestrial is of the earth.

“So also is the resurrection of the dead”: we all have a body, but we’re going to differ from each other. There’s going to be some brothers greater than others; that’s the way it is. Remember what John said about Christ, that he was chosen before him, and Christ said about John that he’s greater than all men. So his body is going to be greater than everybody.
“It is raised in incorruption”: that’s the God body. “It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.”
“The last Adam was made a quickening spirit”: the last Adam is Christ.
“The second man is the Lord from heaven”: he’s telling you that’s the Lord from heaven.
Right now we all have the image of the earthy. When he returns, “we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.”

“Flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God.” “Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep”: meaning we shall not all die, “but we shall all be changed.” Pay close attention to that part: everybody’s not going to be dead when Christ returns.

“In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.” That’s the change, us that are refined as silver.

precepts.why: Awake to righteousness: what is righteousness? “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.” Righteousness is keeping the commandments. So awake to righteousness and sin not is a call to keep the law, and those out there doing secret sins had better stop.

We shall not all sleep: everybody’s not going to be dead when Christ returns. “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first”: because there’s going to be some Israelites that’s already dead.

“Then we which are alive and remain”: there’s going to be a group that’s alive. That’s what we read in Zechariah: that one third is the group that’s going to be alive when Christ returns. So some of us are going to die, and some of us are destined to be alive when Christ returns. “Shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.”

“Wherefore comfort one another with these words.” These are words of comfort. Don’t worry about death; the dead in Christ are going to rise first. When that tribulation really kicks in, when World War Three pops off, don’t be afraid. Understand what’s going to happen.

“And those that be dead will I raise up again from their places, and bring them out of the graves: for I have known my name in Israel.” The Lord already prophesied it: I’m going to raise them up. So the Israelites that die, don’t worry about that; he’s going to raise them up. The dead are going to rise first.

This one is about those that are alive. “And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth”: that’s that one third. “And the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning”: that’s what we just read in 1 Corinthians 15, we shall all be changed.

So all the prophets are saying the same thing over and over and over. Why? To encourage us, to strengthen our faith, so that we can endure the trials and tribulations that are prophesied to come.

sense.text: “Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee”: put the pictures back on the screen; this is what it’s talking about. “Hide thyself as it were for a little moment”: what’s that little moment? Destruction. Just hide yourself, stay inside. Sit by the windows; you can watch. “Until the indignation be overpast”: the indignation is the destruction.

precepts.why: Sit by the windows. “Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?” That’s us, hidden in our chambers while the indignation passes, then flying as a cloud.

This is the part that says come up here. “And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither.” This is what the church always talks about. The great voice is Christ; he says come up hither. “And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”: a cloud is a reference to the chariots of God, what the white man calls UFOs. “And their enemies beheld them.”

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake”: the same time that we’re taken up, brothers and sisters, there’s going to be a great earthquake, destruction. “And the tenth part of the city fell, and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand.”

“And the remnant were affrighted”: that’s why I said sit by the windows like doves. You know a dove is always scared; we’re going to be like those doves beside the window. “And gave glory to the God of heaven”: we’re going to give glory to the God of heaven when this occurs.

sense.text: “And I will bring you out from the people”: that’s what we were reading about. “And will gather you out of the countries wherein ye are scattered, with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out.”

“And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, and there will I plead with you face to face.” “Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt”: he’s letting you know. That’s why Paul said in 1 Corinthians 10 these things were written as examples for us. Why? Because we’re going back.

On the map of the wilderness of the Exodus, you see the wilderness of Egypt, and the first scripture they put on it is Ezekiel 20:36, what we just read. That’s future prophecy. You see all the various places we went to, because remember, we walked for forty years.

“And I will cause you to pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant”: the bond of the covenant is the New Covenant. Yes, we are under the New Covenant right now, but we’re under that portion that’s called grace right now. That’s why a lot of you sin, sin, sin, do whatever the hell you want and speak reckless. But on that day he says no: now you’re under the bond of this New Covenant.

“And I will purge out from among you the rebels”: this is what we read in Zechariah 13 and touched on in Luke 19:27. Some of us in the wilderness are going to rebel. “And them that transgress against me: I will bring them forth out of the country where they sojourn”: some of us are going to come out of America, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, different places.

“And they shall not enter into the land of Israel”: that proves we’re not going to be put in the land of Israel at first; we’re going to be put in the wilderness. “And ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

precepts.why:
Here’s the bond of the covenant. Right now many of us speak reckless; watch this. “In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness.”

“I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered”: ain’t none of the idols that’s here going to be remembered no more. “And also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land”: that’s these reverends, the popes, these fake ministers, the imams. They’re all going to be passed out of the land through destruction.

“When any shall yet prophesy, then his father and his mother that begat him shall say unto him, Thou shalt not live; for thou speakest lies in the name of the Lord: and his father and his mother that begat him shall thrust him through when he prophesieth.” Here’s the bond of the covenant. You have brothers and sisters right now that talk reckless, but watch on this day. That’s the bond: ain’t no more ‘oh I’m sorry, can I repent.’ No.

Christ said the same thing. The Lord ain’t going to play with nobody. Right now everybody is talking, you talk your little smack, you sit home and you murmur; you wait to that day. “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.” That’s what the Son of God says, and that’s about the wilderness.

sense.text: So we’re in the wilderness, and then what? “And make men go over dryshod”: dryshod means having dry shoes or feet. Why does Isaiah say we’re going to go over dryshod? Because he’s going to split the sea again.

“And there shall be an highway for the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria; like as it was to Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.” It’s going to be the same way. Christ is speaking through Isaiah: it’s going to be the same way as when we came out of Egypt.

The whole land of Israel was turned into a wilderness, but it is not the wilderness that we’re going to be taken to, that Ezekiel 20 talks about, and Isaiah 11. “Thou art Gilead unto me, and the head of Lebanon: yet surely I will make thee a wilderness, and cities which are not inhabited.” Gilead and Lebanon were made a wilderness by Babylon. But that is not the wilderness Ezekiel said we’re going back to, that Paul made reference to.

Still talking about Lebanon, here’s what’s going to happen. “The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them”: for the Israelites. “And the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose”: this is when we get to the land.
“The glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon, they shall see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of our God.”
“Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees”: this is for us.

“Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance”: this is what we got to remind brothers and sisters. Fear not; God is coming with vengeance, “even God with a recompence”, with a judgment. “He will come and save you”: God will come and save us.
“Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened”: that’s us. Remember we read in 1 Corinthians 13: we see in part, we know in part, we see through a glass darkly.

“Then shall the lame man leap as an hart”: a deer can leap way higher than a man. It’s letting you know we’re going to be strengthened in that day.

“For in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert”: although Lebanon and Gilead were a wilderness, when we get there, the streams.
“And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water.”

“And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it”: that’s what we just read in Ezekiel, the rebels. Those brothers and sisters with your secret sins, your murmuring: you’re the unclean. You’re not going to enter in. That’s those rebels that are going to be done away with in the wilderness; you’re not going to pass over, you’re not going to get through it.

“But it shall be for those: the wayfaring men”: a wayfaring man is a person traveling on foot.

precepts.why: This is where Paul said we are fools for Christ. “We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak, but ye are strong; ye are honourable, but we are despised.” We are fools for Christ’s sake: the wayfaring men on that highway are these fools for Christ.
“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” See that, making wise the simple: simple is another word for fool. That’s us.
“The Lord preserveth the simple”: that simple there is the fool, the one the Lord preserves. “I was brought low, and he helped me.”

Here’s the wayfaring men explained a little more. “And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel”: how beautiful are the feet of them, because brothers are traveling here and there to preach the gospel, “and bring glad tidings of good things!”

This is an example of wayfaring men: brothers going from city to city teaching the gospel. “And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.”

“And not that only, but who was also chosen of the churches to travel with us with this grace”: see that part, travel with us. What with? With this grace, “which is administered by us to the glory of the same Lord, and declaration of your ready mind”. The wayfaring men travel with the gospel.

“A man that hath travelled knoweth many things”: this is the wayfaring man. You brothers that don’t do no traveling, you’re scared to travel, you know very little. And it ain’t talking about when you used to be in the military, and it ain’t talking about when you and your wife went to Brazil. It’s talking about traveling teaching the gospel.

“And he that hath much experience will declare wisdom. He that hath no experience knoweth little”: you brothers that have no experience know very little, so be quiet. “But he that hath travelled is full of prudence. When I travelled, I saw many things; and I understand more than I can express.”

“He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables. He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes: he will travel through strange countries; for he hath tried the good and the evil among men.”

This is why we’re trying to exhort you men to get your passports, to travel. We need you men to step up and help us preach this gospel throughout all nations.

sense.text: “I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt”: that’s talking about captivity. “And gather them out of Assyria”: captivity. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon”: put that map back up. That’s the land of Israel: you see Lebanon at the very top and Gilead below it in the green. That’s us going into the land, and that’s different than what we read in Ezekiel 20 about the wilderness. “And place shall not be found for them.”

precepts.why:
This explains place shall not be found for them. “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants”. “And they that swallowed thee up shall be far away”: the white man is going to be far away.

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: lost the other means the two thirds that we lost. “Shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: it’s too narrow for us. “Give place to me that I may dwell”: make room, Lord, we need room.

“For the Lord shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places”: why? Because all Israel was wasted. “And he will make her wilderness like Eden”: he’s going to make the wilderness of Israel like Eden, “and her desert like the garden of the Lord”. So it’s going to return back to the time of Adam, the way it was.

“For the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner”: that’s destruction. “But my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished.”

“Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law”: that’s why we got to study and keep the commandments. “Fear ye not the reproach of men”: brothers and sisters, don’t fear what the ADL has to say, the SPLC or Canary Mission; to hell with them. “Neither be ye afraid of their revilings”: don’t be afraid of their hate.

“Thy holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.” Sometimes when you read about the wilderness it’s referring to the land of Israel. Ezekiel 20 and Isaiah 11 are talking about a different wilderness, the one we’re going to walk in dryshod.

Here are the borders of the land. “In the same day the Lord made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt”: that’s the Nile. On the map, everything on the right side of the Nile belongs to Israel. “Unto the great river, the river Euphrates”: you see the river Euphrates highlighted up there where Syria is. All that was given in promise to Abraham, for us.

What you see on the map today as Israel is not the whole land that God gave to our ancestors. “In the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give them, as the days of heaven upon the earth.” “For if ye shall diligently keep all these commandments which I command you, to do them, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cleave unto him; Then will the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and ye shall possess greater nations and mightier than yourselves.”

Now here’s the point: “Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours: from the wilderness”: on the map with the red outline, down at the bottom right after Egypt is the wilderness. “And Lebanon”: you see Lebanon up there. “From the river, the river Euphrates”: that’s up where Syria is. “Even unto the uttermost sea shall your coast be”: the uttermost sea is the Mediterranean on the far left. So God in the Bible has given us the map of our land, given to our forefathers. Lebanon is our land too; the Arabs got it now, and we’re going to take it back.

Gilead is situated in modern day Jordan: today they call it Jordan, the Bible called it Gilead. All that’s ours too, but right now the Arabs got it. The Arabs and the white man got everything, and they’re going to get blown to hell and back.

sense.text: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”: he’s going to bring us back to our land again.

“I will also gather all nations”: this is Armageddon, World War Three. “And will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat”: that’s what we read in Joel when it said their face shall be toward the Dead Sea and the hinder part toward the utmost sea.

“For my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations”: they scattered us in slavery. “And parted my land”: see that part right there. It’s been parted between the Palestinians and the so-called white man.

“And they have cast lots for my people”: they sold us into slavery. “And have given a boy for an harlot”: they made the boys into breeders. “And sold a girl for wine, that they might drink”: young girls, that they could rape them.

“Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon”: those are the Hamites that took the land. “And all the coasts of Palestine”: the Palestinians also took the land. “Swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head”: the Lord’s going to judge them.

The video of the land in 1925 shows it before Edom fully took over the land; they took it over in 1948, but this is 1925, where you had Africans in the land, you had Ishmaelites, Arabs, Palestinians in the land.

precepts.why:
This talks about Idumea taking the land. So we got the Palestinians, they took the land, and who else? “Therefore thus saith the Lord God; Surely in the fire of my jealousy have I spoken against the residue of the heathen, and against all Idumea, which have appointed my land into their possession”.

Idumea, on the screen: pertaining to Edom, the Greek and Roman name for Edom. So that’s the white man, the Caucasians that took the land, that colonized the land. So you got those two groups, the Idumeans and the Palestinians. That’s what the Bible says.

sense.text:
Let’s read about them getting blown to hell and back. Don’t get mad: this is Bible, we’re not speaking out of a racist campaign, we’re giving you what thus saith the Lord.

“Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: that’s a commandment for the Israelites, for us to gather ourselves together.

“Before the decree bring forth”: the decree of destruction. “Before the day pass as the chaff”: before destruction comes. “Before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.”

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment”: stop, see that part, which have wrought his judgments. That’s why we can’t gather with everybody. Some of you want to gather all Israelite camps; all Israelite camps don’t keep the commandments. You’ll hear them lie, steal, commit adultery, all kind of crazy stuff. When it says in verse 1 gather yourselves together, it’s those which have wrought his judgment: which do his commandments.

“Seek righteousness”: seek the commandments. “Seek meekness”: humble yourselves. “It may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” So the only ones we’re looking for in Israel United in Christ are men and women that want to keep the commandments. That’s it. We’re trying to gather ourselves together.

“For Gaza shall be forsaken”: put the map back. God is telling you what he’s going to do to the land: y’all see Gaza right there, with the destruction, the mushroom cloud. “And Ashkelon a desolation”: Ashkelon’s right above Gaza; it’s going to be destroyed. The green is Palestinian, and the beige or yellow is so-called Israel. “They shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day”: that’s Israel, Israelis. “And Ekron shall be rooted up”: that’s Israel too. So the Lord is showing you: I’m going to destroy these places.

“Woe unto the inhabitants of the sea coast”: that’s all those lands along the sea. “The nation of the Cherethites!”: that’s talking about the Palestinians. Write that down: the Palestinians are the Cherethites today. “The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines”: the land of the Palestinians. Philistines and Palestinians is the same word; they just use it differently.

“I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant”: there’s not going to be no inhabitants. This is why he said Gilead is mine, Lebanon, I’m going to take you back. You’re going back there because all the inhabitants are going to be wiped away.
“And the sea coast shall be dwellings and cottages for shepherds”: that’s when we enter the land; we’re going to take that sea coast over.

“And the coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah”: Judah’s going to take that whole sea coast. “For the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity”: he’s going to turn away our captivity. That’s some heavy stuff.

We always read verse 18, but today we’re going to keep reading. “And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them”: they’re going to get burnt up. “And devour them”: we’re going to devour them. “And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” The Lord spoke that thing.

This is when there’s going to be peace on earth, good will toward men: when Esau is wiped out. But guess what, it ain’t over.

“And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau”: put the map with the red lines back up. The mount of Esau is down at the bottom, where it says Edom, and above it the Amalekites. We’re going to possess that. “And they of the plain the Philistines”: we’re going to take that side too. “And they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria”: we’re going to take that back. “And Benjamin shall possess Gilead”: Gilead’s at the top.

“And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites”: possess means own. We’re going to possess the Hamites. “Shall possess the cities of the south”: we’re going to possess the cities of the south.
“And saviours shall come up on mount Zion”: the saviours are the 144,000. “To judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.”

“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”: yet choose us as his people. “And set them in their own land”: he’s going to set us in our own land; we’re going to go over dryshod. “And the strangers shall be joined with them”: there are going to be strange nations there with us. “And they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: they’re going to keep the commandments through us.

“And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids”: look at the pictures. Don’t get mad, that’s what the Bible says. Don’t get mad at us. All I can say to you other nations: you better pray you got the blood of Israel in you, because that’s the only way you’re going to make it. If you’re not, you know what’s coming for you, so you better shut your mouth.

“And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear”: we’ve got to speak this to our sister Tiffany Carter, whose son Rasheem Carter had his head cut off and his spine removed, and to George Floyd’s mother and father. Our brothers and sisters are sitting there in sorrow, and we see this stuff. The Lord is going to give us rest from our sorrow and from our fear.

Don’t get mad at us; get mad at God. “He that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.” All we got to do is be patient.
